pr.author: cjgillot

processing.reason: The supplied PR is an optimization refactor of `RemoveNoopLandingPads` that separates no-op landing-pad discovery from CFG mutation to avoid repeatedly clearing the CFG cache. The frozen analysis explicitly states there is no source evidence that the old one-loop order miscompiled, and it instructs not to construct a semantically wrong old/new rewrite for this PR. The historical source at the PR head confirms the change is only discovery/mutation ordering plus `#[instrument]`/debug-message adjustments, with no changed value semantics or regression test demonstrating a miscompile. Therefore no source-grounded historically incorrect transformation can be encoded, and manufacturing an unrelated rewrite would violate the task constraints.

analysis.originalLogic: `RemoveNoopLandingPads::run_pass` used a single post-order loop over `traversal::postorder(body)`. For each block it first changed matching `UnwindAction::Cleanup` edges to `UnwindAction::Continue` and redirected matching successors to `resume_block`, then called `is_nop_landing_pad(bb, body, &nop_landing_pads)` on the already-mutated body and inserted `bb` into the no-op set. The PR describes this as "Refactor remove_noop_landing_pads in two loops. The point is to avoid clearing the CFG cache as often."
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historical implementation was an interleaved discovery-and-mutation strategy: cleanup edges were folded while the pass was still computing which landing pads are no-ops, via repeated `body[bb]` mutable accesses. The patch moves all no-op discovery to a first immutable post-order loop and all edge rewrites to a second loop using `body.basic_blocks.as_mut()` and `iter_enumerated_mut()`. There is no source evidence that the old order miscompiled; this is a performance refactor to reduce CFG-cache clearing, not a confirmed bug fix. Do not construct a semantically wrong old/new rewrite for this PR.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR for unwind-capable functions (the pass is required when `sess.panic_strategy().unwinds()`) that contains at least one `TerminatorKind::UnwindResume` and has cleanup edges (`UnwindAction::Cleanup`) targeting candidate landing pads. Candidate pads contain only ignorable statements and allowed terminators, with successors that are themselves already-known no-op landing pads or the resume block. Include nested no-op landing-pad chains, bodies with no resume block, and bodies where the discovered no-op set is empty.
analysis.summary: Optimization refactor of Rust MIR `RemoveNoopLandingPads`: separate no-op landing-pad discovery from CFG mutation to avoid repeatedly clearing the CFG cache. Correctness depends on preserving post-order discovery so nested landing pads are recognized before predecessors, and on performing the later rewrite over the same already-discovered set.
analysis.trigger: A MIR body has unwind cleanup edges into one or more no-op landing-pad blocks. The pass should first discover all such pads in post-order on the untouched body, then fold cleanup edges and successors to the resume block.
preconditions: The pass only runs when unwind handling is enabled for the panic strategy.
The body must contain a `TerminatorKind::UnwindResume`; otherwise the refactored pass returns early.
No-op classification must still use post-order traversal so that if A post-dominates B, A is classified before B.
Mutation should be deferred until after all no-op pads are collected, or it must not invalidate classification of the current block.
An empty no-op landing-pad set should return before creating or applying any resume-block patch.
pitfalls: This PR is not evidence of a semantic bug; treating the old one-loop order as a known miscompile would invent a wrong rewrite.
Changing the discovery traversal from post-order to another order can classify nested landing pads incorrectly because outer pads depend on already-known inner pads.
Recomputing `nop_landing_pads` after edges have been folded risks changing which blocks qualify, instead of using the set discovered on the original body.
Mutating through per-block `body[bb]` accessors can repeatedly invalidate the CFG cache; the refactor instead takes `body.basic_blocks.as_mut()` once for the rewrite loop.
The early return for an empty no-op set must occur before the resume-block patch path to retain the intended work avoidance.
`#[instrument]` and changed debug messages are observability-only and must not be treated as semantic changes.
analysis.testStrategy: Use focused MIR tests or `-Zunpretty=mir` comparisons on panic-unwind programs that create nested cleanup paths, for example nested values with destructors and calls that can unwind. Verify that every cleanup edge targeting a known no-op landing pad is folded and that nested pads are still discovered in post-order. Include negative cases with no `UnwindResume` and with no qualifying landing pads to exercise the new early returns. Differential testing should compare MIR before and after the refactor for equivalence of cleanup removal and successor folding, not runtime behavior; no regression test changes are present in the supplied patch, so do not claim such a test was run.
evidence: The point is to avoid clearing the CFG cache as often.
This is a post-order traversal, so that if A post-dominates B
then A will be visited before B.
